title: SKF India (Industrial) Ltd - 544572 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: SKF India (Industrial) Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28.3% YoY to INR10,429 million, with PBT margin at 12.9% (up 42 bps).
summary.overview: Revenue grew 28.3% YoY to INR10,429 million, with wind, heavy industries, exports and distribution leading. PBT was about INR1,344 million (12.9% margin), up 42 bps, helped by absence of last year's one-off demerger costs and a forex gain, offset by steel, oil and logistics inflation. Operating cash flow was negative at INR61 million, which management attributed to clearing intercompany payables; H1 cash conversion was stated at 19.5%. Management said Ahmedabad CRB capacity is ramping and the new Pune plant is expected to be up by 2028.

financial_highlights.change: PBT up about 32.6% YoY in absolute terms
Cash conversion -4.5%; management called it one-off
Wind about 40%+, heavy industries about 30%+, distribution 8-10%
Analyst figure; management did not dispute it, said it will revisit guidance basis

segments.name: Wind
segments.commentary: H1 growth about 40%+ YoY; management says wind revenue and its share of revenue are at record highs, with the most wind capacity in the market.

segments.name: Heavy industries
segments.commentary: H1 growth about 30%+ YoY on strong project orders; material handling and off-highway are key drivers, and management claims share gains above industry growth.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: H1 growth about 8-10% YoY; management says it is growing 2-3% above GDP. Also described as the most broad-based business.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share of OE sales rose from about 12% to 16% QoQ, enabled by the TRB line added at the Pune factory.

segments.name: Rail
segments.commentary: Declining, as government shifts spending from rolling stock to tracks.

segments.name: OE mix
segments.commentary: GM 26% of OE (13% of total), wind 16%, rail 17%, heavy industries 16%, agri and electrical 14% (new segment), metals 11%.

guidance_outlook: Management says it aims to grow above GDP; no annual FY28 revenue guidance was given when asked.
PBT margin is the company's guided metric (12-13% cited by analyst); management said it will revisit whether to guide on EBITDA.
IT and demerger one-offs expected to largely nullify by end of Q3 FY27.
Ahmedabad expansion: about 2 full channels and 1 roller channel expected in the next year; management expects about 15% higher growth in addressed markets from these channels.
Pune new plant expected to be up and running by end-2028.
Management expects a steel-driven cost hit from Chinese imports (about 55% of products are imported) in the next quarter or two.
capex_capacity: Ahmedabad: new medium CRB line inaugurated in Q2, adding about 220,000 units annual capacity for gearbox, motors, railway, agri and aftermarket.
Pune: TRB line added last quarter; part of its capacity allocated to exports.
Ahmedabad: about 2 full channels and 1 roller channel expected in the next year.
New Pune plant: investment in progress, expected to be completed in 2028.
Localization: a large bearing that took about 8 months to import is now supplied locally in about 2 months.
demand_pricing: Industrial production growth at 7.1%, the strongest in a while; construction expected to grow about 10% YoY.
Steel prices up about 15-16% over the last three quarters, driven by Middle East impact; price increases were taken through the year with OEM and distributor customers.
Management said cost inflation is from steel, oil, logistics and heat treatment; further price actions are possible if steel, oil or rupee moves adversely.
Market share: 19.4-19.5% for FY25 (up 0.2-0.3 pts); FY26 study not yet done.
Freight segment expected to moderate after strength up to last quarter.
Rail declining as government shifts spending from rolling stock to tracks.

qa_highlights.question: Was there forex or IT cost in the quarter, and how much further cost and pricing impact is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: FX was positive because the rupee appreciated at end-September. IT costs were lower than last year and expected to nullify by end-Q3. Price increases have been taken through the year, with further actions possible if steel, oil or rupee moves worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses rose QoQ; what drove the increase after adjusting for one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a write-off of old receivables of about INR60 million (provided earlier, with the release in other income), higher logistics costs, and legal and professional fees for a cost-efficiency consultant project. A Q1 vs Q2 reconciliation was disputed by an analyst and taken offline.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the other-expense gap versus Q1, and what is the demerger cost in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Demerger-related expense was about INR100 million in Q2 against about INR160 million in Q1. Management said the QoQ change in other operating expenses is minor, with some increases in miscellaneous and logistics.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook, and why guide on PBT rather than EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: The analyst calculated a Q2 EBITDA margin of about 9.6% including other income. Management attributed the gap to higher other income from forex gains and said it would revisit whether EBITDA guidance is more appropriate.

qa_highlights.question: Will more Ahmedabad lines come before the new Pune plant, and what is their revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: About 2 full channels and 1 roller channel are expected in Ahmedabad in the next year. Management would not give a revenue figure, but expects about 15% higher growth in addressed markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pathway to a 14% margin, and is 13-14% the steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 PBT margin is close to 13% after excluding FX and one-off demerger costs, versus about 9% in Q1, so 13-14% is the steady-state margin before manufacturing efficiencies kick in.

risks_watch: Steel cost inflation (about 15-16%) and Chinese steel import prices, with a possible negative impact over the next one to two quarters.
Oil, logistics and rupee moves could erode margins further if not offset by price increases.
Other expenses rose QoQ (write-offs, logistics, consultant fees); the reconciliation was taken offline.
Rail decline and expected freight moderation.
Execution risk on the Pune plant (end-2028) and Ahmedabad channels.
Cash conversion was negative in Q2; management expects a rebound and a working capital level of about 19%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and growth, citing record wind revenue and strong heavy industries. More cautious on margins and costs, with a qualified steel and currency outlook. Evasive on the EBITDA-versus-PBT guidance question and on FY28 revenue guidance.
key_quotes: We have partially offset these costs with improved price realization.
So this is a one-off, and you see our cash conversion at minus 4.5%.
This is a large bearing which would typically take about 8 months to be produced and reach India, and we're now able to do that within 2 months.
Historically, we have been measuring ourselves on PBT, right?

adds.what: Ahmedabad medium CRB line adding about 220,000 units/yr (gearbox, motors, railway, agri, aftermarket)
Ahmedabad about 2 full channels and 1 roller channel

growth.why: No annual FY28 revenue guidance given; management only says it aims to grow above GDP, with H1 FY27 revenue up about 20% driven by wind (+40%+) and heavy industries (+30%+), backed by the commissioned Ahmedabad CRB line (~220,000 units/yr) and Pune TRB line, while the new Pune plant has slipped to end-2028 and the Ahmedabad channels are due in about a year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 PBT margin 12.9% (+42 bps YoY) and management says ~13% ex-FX and demerger costs, with 13-14% steady state before manufacturing efficiencies, but steel up ~15-16% and Chinese import cost hit expected in next 1-2 quarters.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Ahmedabad medium CRB line (~220,000 units/yr) already commissioned and about 2 full channels plus 1 roller channel due within a year; new Pune plant under construction for end-2028, so only the Ahmedabad adds land inside the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue up about 20% YoY with wind up 40%+ and heavy industries up 30%+, and industrial production growth at 7.1%; distribution slower at 8-10%, rail declining, freight expected to moderate.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation not disclosed, but capacity additions are already committed (Pune to 2028, Ahmedabad channels in a year), and management has not signalled a new capex beyond these.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No annual FY28 revenue guidance given and management only aims to grow above GDP; cost inflation and steel headwinds argue against raising guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects a steel-driven cost hit from Chinese imports (about 55% of products imported) and steel prices are up ~15-16% over three quarters, with further price actions possible if steel, oil or rupee moves adversely.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or model launch was discussed beyond the capacity lines; the agri and electrical segment is described as new but no launch timing was given.

rows.label: GM localisation to 70-75% by 2028
rows.why: Management targets 70-75% localisation in general machinery by 2028 and a large bearing that took ~8 months to import is now supplied locally in ~2 months.

rows.label: Cash conversion rebound and NWC near 19%
rows.why: Q2 operating cash flow was INR-61 million (cash conversion -4.5%) and H1 conversion 19.5%; management expects a rebound with NWC around 19% of revenue, but NWC is already 18.9% and up 25.8%.

rows.label: Export share rising on Pune TRB line
rows.why: Export share of OE sales rose from about 12% to 16% QoQ, enabled by the TRB line at Pune with part of its capacity allocated to exports.

tone.note: Management was confident on wind (record revenue, up 40%+ in H1) and heavy industries (up 30%+), but cautious on steel, oil and currency costs and evasive on the EBITDA-versus-PBT guidance basis and FY28 revenue guidance; analysts pushed on other-expense rise QoQ, the demerger cost reconciliation an

oneOffs.what: Year-ago Q2 carried one-off demerger costs; their absence helped PBT growth, so the comparison flatters Q2 profit (demerger expense about INR100 million in Q2 vs INR160 million in Q1)
FX gain in Q2 FY27 from rupee appreciation at end-September, helping PBT; management said Q2 PBT margin is about 13% excluding FX and one-off demerger costs
About INR60 million write-off of old receivables in Q2 other expenses, partly offset by release in other income

quality.why: Revenue grew 28.3% YoY to INR10,429 million, led by wind, heavy industries and exports with H1 growth about 20%, which looks recurring, but the PBT growth of about 32.6% and 42 bps margin expansion are flattered by absence of last year's demerger costs and a forex gain, while a ~INR60 million receivable write-off and negative Q2 operating cash flow weigh the other way.
